subject: mark-resight: variance estimation fails when estimating/fixing pID

messages.author: a24d06844d361733
messages.subject: mark-resight: variance estimation fails when estimating/fixing pID
parts:
Hi all, 

I have a singular session, mark-resight dataset. 12% of detections were of marked individuals which could not be identified. 

When I leave secr to estimate the proportion of identified individuals, variance estimation fails (NA's everywhere...). 
When I fix pID to 0.88 (or any other number), variance estimation also fails. 

I have tried all the usual trouble shooting routes for failed variance calculations (different starting values, methods etc), but alas, no success. 
Anyone know why this is happening / if it's fixable? 

Cheers,
Matt.

messages.subject: Re: mark-resight: variance estimation fails when estimating/fixing pID
parts: Bayesian SMR fun-fact for those who are interested. When the density of marked individuals on the landscape is low, knowing the spatial location of the sample carries a lot of information about their individual identity, much more so than for the unmarked individuals who are typically more dense given typical marking rates. Jose Jimenez has a paper under review demonstrating this. If the density of marked individuals is low enough, it's possible that knowing the spatial location of marked but no identity samples effectively tells you who they are with certainty.
